title: Professional Git Workflow with CI/CD
description: Set up a professional Python project with pre-commit hooks, a README with badges, GitHub Actions CI, and a complete PR workflow
objective: Students will set up a Python project with proper structure, configure pre-commit hooks for automated code quality, write a professional README with badges, create a GitHub Actions CI pipeline, and complete a full pull request workflow with code review

steps.title: Set Up a Python Project with Proper Structure
steps.instructions:
## Create the Project

Open your terminal and create a new project:

```bash
mkdir techpath-course-manager
cd techpath-course-manager
git init
```

## Create the Folder Structure

Create the following structure:

```
techpath-course-manager/
|-- app/
|   |-- __init__.py
|   |-- main.py
|   |-- models.py
|   |-- utils.py
|-- tests/
|   |-- __init__.py
|   |-- test_models.py
|   |-- test_utils.py
|-- .gitignore
|-- requirements.txt
|-- README.md
```

Create the directories:

```bash
mkdir app tests
```

Create empty `__init__.py` files (these make Python treat folders as packages):

```bash
touch app/__init__.py tests/__init__.py
```

On Windows (if `touch` doesn't work), create empty files in VS Code.

## Add the Code

Create `app/models.py`:

```python
from dataclasses import dataclass


@dataclass
class Student:
    name: str
    roll_number: str
    course: str
    city: str
    fee: float

    def display(self):
        return f"{self.name} ({self.roll_number}) - {self.course}, {self.city}"


@dataclass
class Course:
    name: str
    duration_months: int
    fee: float

    def fee_with_gst(self):
        gst_rate = 0.18
        return round(self.fee * (1 + gst_rate), 2)

    def monthly_emi(self):
        return round(self.fee_with_gst() / self.duration_months, 2)
```

Create `app/utils.py`:

```python
def format_currency(amount):
    return f"Rs. {amount:,.2f}"


def validate_email(email):
    if not isinstance(email, str):
        return False
    return "@" in email and "." in email.split("@")[-1]


def calculate_grade(percentage):
    if percentage >= 90:
        return "A+"
    elif percentage >= 80:
        return "A"
    elif percentage >= 70:
        return "B"
    elif percentage >= 60:
        return "C"
    elif percentage >= 50:
        return "D"
    else:
        return "F"
```

Create `app/main.py`:

```python
from app.models import Course, Student
from app.utils import calculate_grade, format_currency


def main():
    # Create sample students
    students = [
        Student("Rahul Sharma", "TP2026001", "ADCA", "Bhopal", 35000),
        Student("Priya Patel", "TP2026002", "Python Mastery", "Indore", 12000),
        Student("Amit Verma", "TP2026003", "Web Development", "Delhi", 20000),
    ]

    # Create a course
    course = Course("ADCA", 12, 35000)

    print("=== TechPath Institute - Course Manager ===")
    print()

    for student in students:
        print(student.display())

    print()
    print(f"Course: {course.name}")
    print(f"Fee: {format_currency(course.fee)}")
    print(f"Fee with GST: {format_currency(course.fee_with_gst())}")
    print(f"Monthly EMI: {format_currency(course.monthly_emi())}")
    print()
    print(f"85% -> Grade: {calculate_grade(85)}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

Create `tests/test_models.py`:

```python
from app.models import Course, Student


def test_student_display():
    student = Student("Rahul Sharma", "TP001", "ADCA", "Bhopal", 35000)
    assert "Rahul Sharma" in student.display()
    assert "TP001" in student.display()


def test_course_fee_with_gst():
    course = Course("ADCA", 12, 10000)
    assert course.fee_with_gst() == 11800.0


def test_course_monthly_emi():
    course = Course("DCA", 6, 18000)
    total = course.fee_with_gst()
    emi = course.monthly_emi()
    assert emi == round(total / 6, 2)
```

Create `tests/test_utils.py`:

```python
from app.utils import calculate_grade, format_currency, validate_email


def test_format_currency():
    assert format_currency(15999.50) == "Rs. 15,999.50"
    assert format_currency(0) == "Rs. 0.00"


def test_validate_email_valid():
    assert validate_email("rahul@techpath.biz") is True
    assert validate_email("priya@gmail.com") is True


def test_validate_email_invalid():
    assert validate_email("not-an-email") is False
    assert validate_email("") is False
    assert validate_email(123) is False


def test_calculate_grade():
    assert calculate_grade(95) == "A+"
    assert calculate_grade(85) == "A"
    assert calculate_grade(75) == "B"
    assert calculate_grade(65) == "C"
    assert calculate_grade(55) == "D"
    assert calculate_grade(40) == "F"
```

Create `requirements.txt`:

```
pytest>=8.0.0
ruff>=0.5.0
black>=24.4.0
isort>=5.13.0
pre-commit>=3.7.0
```

Create `.gitignore`:

```
__pycache__/
*.pyc
.venv/
.env
.vscode/
*.db
.pytest_cache/
htmlcov/
.coverage
.mypy_cache/
```

## Install Dependencies

```bash
python -m venv .venv
# Windows:
.venv\Scripts\activate
# Mac/Linux:
# source .venv/bin/activate

pip install -r requirements.txt
```

## Verify Tests Pass

```bash
pytest -v
```

All tests should pass. Stage and commit:

```bash
git add .
git commit -m "feat: initialize course manager project with tests"
```

steps.title: Add Pre-commit Hooks (ruff, black, isort)
steps.instructions:
## Create the Pre-commit Config

Create a file called `.pre-commit-config.yaml` in the project root:

```yaml
repos:
  # Ruff — fast Python linter and formatter
  - repo: https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff-pre-commit
    rev: v0.5.0
    hooks:
      - id: ruff
        args: [--fix]
      - id: ruff-format

  # Black — code formatter
  - repo: https://github.com/psf/black
    rev: 24.4.2
    hooks:
      - id: black

  # isort — sort imports
  - repo: https://github.com/pycqa/isort
    rev: 5.13.2
    hooks:
      - id: isort
        args: ["--profile", "black"]

  # General file checks
  - repo: https://github.com/pre-commit/pre-commit-hooks
    rev: v4.6.0
    hooks:
      - id: trailing-whitespace
      - id: end-of-file-fixer
      - id: check-yaml
      - id: check-added-large-files
```

## Install the Hooks

```bash
pre-commit install
```

You should see: `pre-commit installed at .git/hooks/pre-commit`

This means every time you run `git commit`, these checks will run automatically.

## Test the Hooks

Let's intentionally create a messy file to see hooks in action.

Create `app/messy_example.py` with intentionally bad code:

```python
import os
import sys
import json
from pathlib import Path
from collections import OrderedDict
import  random

def   calculate_discount(price,discount_percent  ):
    """Calculate discounted price for TechPath courses."""
    if discount_percent>100 or discount_percent<0:
        return price
    discount_amount=price*discount_percent/100
    final_price=price-discount_amount
    return final_price

def   get_student_info( name,city,course   ):
    info = {  "name":name,"city":city,
    "course":course,"institute":"TechPath Institute"  }
    return info
```

Now try to commit it:

```bash
git add app/messy_example.py
git commit -m "test: add messy code to test pre-commit"
```

You should see output like:

```
ruff.....................................................Failed
ruff-format..............................................Failed
black....................................................Failed
isort....................................................Passed
trailing-whitespace......................................Failed
end-of-file-fixer........................................Failed
check-yaml...............................................Passed
check-added-large-files..................................Passed
```

The commit is BLOCKED! But ruff and black have auto-fixed most issues.

## Review and Commit the Fixed Code

Check what changed:

```bash
git diff app/messy_example.py
```

The formatters removed unused imports (`os`, `sys`, `json`, `Path`, `OrderedDict`, `random`), fixed spacing, and cleaned up the code.

Stage and try to commit again:

```bash
git add app/messy_example.py
git commit -m "test: add messy code to test pre-commit"
```

This time all hooks should PASS and the commit goes through.

Now commit the pre-commit config:

```bash
git add .pre-commit-config.yaml
git commit -m "chore: add pre-commit hooks for ruff, black, isort"
```

Delete the messy example file and commit:

```bash
rm app/messy_example.py
git add app/messy_example.py
git commit -m "chore: remove test messy file"
```

Take a screenshot of the pre-commit output showing hooks failing and then passing.

steps.title: Write a Professional README with Badges
steps.instructions:
## Replace Your README

Open `README.md` and replace its content with a professional README:

```markdown
# TechPath Course Manager

A Python application to manage courses, students, and fee calculations at TechPath Institute.

![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.11-blue)
![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-green)
![Code Style](https://img.shields.io/badge/code%20style-black-000000)
![Linter](https://img.shields.io/badge/linter-ruff-D7FF64)

## Features

- Student registration with name, roll number, course, and city
- Course fee calculation with 18% GST
- Monthly EMI calculation
- Grade calculation from percentage
- Email validation
- Indian Rupee currency formatting

## Tech Stack

- **Language:** Python 3.11
- **Testing:** pytest
- **Linting:** ruff
- **Formatting:** black, isort
- **CI/CD:** GitHub Actions

## Installation

### Prerequisites

- Python 3.11 or higher
- pip (Python package manager)
- Git

### Steps

```bash
# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/YOUR-USERNAME/techpath-course-manager.git
cd techpath-course-manager

# Create and activate virtual environment
python -m venv .venv
# Windows:
.venv\Scripts\activate
# Mac/Linux:
source .venv/bin/activate

# Install dependencies
pip install -r requirements.txt

# Set up pre-commit hooks
pre-commit install
```

## Usage

```bash
python -m app.main
```

Output:
```
=== TechPath Institute - Course Manager ===

Rahul Sharma (TP2026001) - ADCA, Bhopal
Priya Patel (TP2026002) - Python Mastery, Indore
Amit Verma (TP2026003) - Web Development, Delhi

Course: ADCA
Fee: Rs. 35,000.00
Fee with GST: Rs. 41,300.00
Monthly EMI: Rs. 3,441.67

85% -> Grade: A
```

## Running Tests

```bash
# Run all tests
pytest -v

# Run with coverage
pytest --cov=app
```

## Project Structure

```
techpath-course-manager/
|-- app/
|   |-- __init__.py
|   |-- main.py          # Entry point
|   |-- models.py        # Student and Course data models
|   |-- utils.py         # Helper functions
|-- tests/
|   |-- __init__.py
|   |-- test_models.py   # Tests for models
|   |-- test_utils.py    # Tests for utilities
|-- .github/
|   |-- workflows/
|       |-- ci.yml       # GitHub Actions CI pipeline
|-- .gitignore
|-- .pre-commit-config.yaml
|-- requirements.txt
|-- README.md
```

## Contributing

1. Fork the repository
2. Create a feature branch (`git switch -c feature/your-feature`)
3. Commit your changes using conventional commits
4. Push to the branch (`git push -u origin feature/your-feature`)
5. Open a Pull Request

## License

MIT License
```

Replace `YOUR-USERNAME` with your actual GitHub username.

## Commit the README

```bash
git add README.md
git commit -m "docs: add professional README with badges and structure"
```

## Explore Shields.io

Visit [shields.io](https://shields.io/) and try creating custom badges:

1. Go to shields.io
2. Try the **Static Badge** option
3. Enter Label: `institute`, Message: `TechPath`, Color: `purple`
4. Copy the markdown and add it to your README

The badge URL format is:
```
https://img.shields.io/badge/LABEL-MESSAGE-COLOR
```

Spaces in the message use `%20` or `_`.

steps.title: Create a GitHub Actions Workflow
steps.instructions:
## Create the Workflow Directory

GitHub Actions looks for workflow files in `.github/workflows/`. Create the folder:

```bash
mkdir -p .github/workflows
```

On Windows (if `mkdir -p` doesn't work):

```bash
mkdir .github
mkdir .github\workflows
```

## Create the Workflow File

Create `.github/workflows/ci.yml`:

```yaml
name: TechPath CI Pipeline

# Run on push to main/develop and on pull requests to main
on:
  push:
    branches: [main, develop]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  lint-and-test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      # Get the code
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # Install Python
      - name: Set up Python 3.11
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"

      # Cache packages for faster runs
      - name: Cache pip packages
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/pip
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-pip-${{ hashFiles('requirements.txt') }}

      # Install dependencies
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          pip install -r requirements.txt

      # Lint
      - name: Lint with ruff
        run: ruff check .

      # Format check
      - name: Check formatting with black
        run: black --check .

      # Tests
      - name: Run tests
        run: pytest -v
```

## Commit the Workflow

```bash
git add .github/workflows/ci.yml
git commit -m "ci: add GitHub Actions pipeline for linting and testing"
```

## Push to GitHub

Create a repository on GitHub called `techpath-course-manager`, then:

```bash
git remote add origin https://github.com/YOUR-USERNAME/techpath-course-manager.git
git push -u origin main
```

## Watch It Run

1. Go to your repository on GitHub
2. Click the **Actions** tab
3. You should see your workflow running (or just completed)
4. Click on the run to see detailed logs for each step
5. A green checkmark means all steps passed

Take a screenshot of the Actions tab showing a passing run.

## Add the CI Badge to README

GitHub automatically provides a badge for your workflow. Add it to the top of your README:

```markdown
![CI](https://github.com/YOUR-USERNAME/techpath-course-manager/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)
```

This badge will show "passing" (green) or "failing" (red) in real-time.

```bash
git add README.md
git commit -m "docs: add CI status badge to README"
git push
```

steps.title: Complete PR Workflow with Code Review
steps.instructions:
## Create a Feature Branch

Now let's do a complete professional workflow — feature branch, PR, CI check, and merge.

```bash
# Make sure main is up to date
git switch main
git pull

# Create a feature branch
git switch -c feature/add-enrollment
```

## Add the New Feature

Create `app/enrollment.py`:

```python
from datetime import datetime

from app.models import Course, Student
from app.utils import format_currency, validate_email


def enroll_student(name, email, course_name, city):
    """Enroll a student in a course at TechPath Institute."""
    if not validate_email(email):
        raise ValueError(f"Invalid email: {email}")

    # Generate roll number based on current date
    year = datetime.now().year
    roll = f"TP{year}{datetime.now().strftime('%m%d%H%M')}"

    student = Student(
        name=name,
        roll_number=roll,
        course=course_name,
        city=city,
        fee=0,  # Will be set from course
    )
    return student


def print_enrollment_receipt(student, course):
    """Print a formatted enrollment receipt."""
    fee_with_gst = course.fee_with_gst()
    print("=" * 45)
    print("   TECHPATH INSTITUTE - ENROLLMENT RECEIPT")
    print("=" * 45)
    print(f"  Student:  {student.name}")
    print(f"  Roll No:  {student.roll_number}")
    print(f"  Course:   {course.name}")
    print(f"  Duration: {course.duration_months} months")
    print(f"  City:     {student.city}")
    print("-" * 45)
    print(f"  Fee:      {format_currency(course.fee)}")
    print(f"  GST (18%):{format_currency(fee_with_gst - course.fee)}")
    print(f"  Total:    {format_currency(fee_with_gst)}")
    print(f"  EMI:      {format_currency(course.monthly_emi())}/month")
    print("=" * 45)
```

Create `tests/test_enrollment.py`:

```python
import pytest

from app.enrollment import enroll_student


def test_enroll_student_valid():
    student = enroll_student(
        name="Neha Gupta",
        email="neha@techpath.biz",
        course_name="Python Mastery",
        city="Hyderabad",
    )
    assert student.name == "Neha Gupta"
    assert student.city == "Hyderabad"
    assert student.roll_number.startswith("TP")


def test_enroll_student_invalid_email():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        enroll_student(
            name="Vikram Singh",
            email="not-valid",
            course_name="ADCA",
            city="Bhopal",
        )


def test_enroll_student_roll_number_format():
    student = enroll_student(
        name="Ananya Reddy",
        email="ananya@gmail.com",
        course_name="Web Dev",
        city="Pune",
    )
    assert student.roll_number.startswith("TP2026")
    assert len(student.roll_number) > 6
```

## Run Tests Locally

```bash
pytest -v
```

All tests should pass.

## Commit and Push

```bash
git add app/enrollment.py tests/test_enrollment.py
git commit -m "feat: add student enrollment with receipt generation"
git push -u origin feature/add-enrollment
```

## Create a Pull Request

1. Go to GitHub and click **Compare & pull request**
2. Title: `feat: add student enrollment feature`
3. Description:

```markdown
## What does this PR do?
Adds student enrollment functionality with receipt generation.

## Changes
- Added `app/enrollment.py` with `enroll_student()` and `print_enrollment_receipt()`
- Added `tests/test_enrollment.py` with 3 test cases
- Auto-generates roll numbers in TP2026MMDDHHMM format
- Validates email before enrollment
- Receipt includes fee breakdown with GST

## How to Test
```bash
pytest tests/test_enrollment.py -v
```

## Checklist
- [x] Tests pass
- [x] Code formatted with black
- [x] Linted with ruff
- [x] Conventional commit used
```

4. Click **Create pull request**

## Watch the CI Pipeline

GitHub Actions will automatically run your CI pipeline on this PR:
1. Click the **Checks** tab on the PR
2. Watch the pipeline run
3. Wait for all checks to pass (green checkmarks)

## Code Review (Pair Up)

If possible, pair up with a classmate:
1. Share your repository link
2. Add them as a collaborator: Settings -> Collaborators -> Add
3. They open your PR, go to **Files changed** tab
4. They leave a comment on one line (click the `+` icon next to a line number)
5. They submit a review: Approve or Request Changes

If working alone, leave a self-review comment on the PR.

## Merge the PR

1. After the CI pipeline passes, click **Squash and merge**
2. Edit the merge commit message if needed
3. Click **Confirm squash and merge**
4. Click **Delete branch**

## Pull Changes Locally

```bash
git switch main
git pull
git branch -d feature/add-enrollment
```

## Verify

```bash
# Run all tests one final time
pytest -v

# Check the full log
git log --oneline
```

Congratulations! You have completed a full professional Git workflow with pre-commit hooks, CI/CD, and code review.
